treatments.name: Calcium channel blockers
treatments.population: Adults with hypertension (randomised trials of first-line therapy)
treatments.summary: First-line CCBs show no difference in all-cause mortality versus other classes; they probably reduce major cardiovascular events more than beta-blockers but less than diuretics.

evidence.quote: All-cause mortality was not different between first-line CCBs and any other antihypertensive classes.
evidence.statement: First-line CCBs did not differ from other classes on all-cause mortality.

evidence.quote: There is low to moderate certainty evidence that CCBs probably reduce major cardiovascular events more than beta-blockers.
evidence.statement: CCBs probably reduce major cardiovascular events more than beta-blockers.

evidence.quote: Many of the differences found in the current review are not robust, and further trials might change the conclusions.
evidence.statement: Many between-class differences are not robust and may change with further trials.

treatments.name: Diuretics
treatments.population: Adults with hypertension (randomised trials of first-line therapy)
treatments.summary: Diuretics reduce major cardiovascular events and congestive heart failure more than CCBs.

evidence.quote: For the treatment of hypertension, there is moderate certainty evidence that diuretics reduce major cardiovascular events and congestive heart failure more than CCBs.
evidence.statement: Diuretics reduce major cardiovascular events and heart failure more than CCBs.

treatments.name: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers
treatments.population: Adults with hypertension (randomised trials of first-line therapy)
treatments.summary: Compared with CCBs, ACE inhibitors and ARBs were associated with less congestive heart failure, while CCBs reduced stroke versus ACE inhibitors and myocardial infarction versus ARBs.

evidence.quote: There is low to moderate certainty evidence that CCBs reduced stroke when compared to angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and reduced myocardial infarction when compared to angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), but increased congestive heart failure when compared to ACE inhibitors and ARBs.
evidence.statement: ACE inhibitors and ARBs had fewer heart failure events than CCBs; CCBs had fewer strokes (vs ACE inhibitors) and myocardial infarctions (vs ARBs).

treatments.name: Beta-blockers
treatments.population: Adults with hypertension (randomised trials of first-line therapy)
treatments.summary: Beta-blockers performed worse than CCBs as first-line therapy for major cardiovascular events, stroke and cardiovascular mortality.

evidence.quote: As compared to beta-blockers, CCBs reduced the following outcomes: major cardiovascular events (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77 to 0.92), stroke (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.88, moderate-certainty evidence), and cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.99, low-certainty evidence).
evidence.statement: Compared with beta-blockers, CCBs reduced major cardiovascular events, stroke and cardiovascular mortality.
